overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on any of the four allegations, and closed the complaint as resolved with no orders.

allegations.summary: Commission allegedly closed its June 12 meeting while an issue was on the floor.
allegations.key_passage: First, there is no directive in the Open Meeting Law as to when a public body may end a meeting.

allegations.summary: Two Commission members allegedly conspired outside an open meeting to remove a member from the Commission.
allegations.key_passage: Even if the alleged communication between two Commission members occurred outside of an open meeting, therefore, it would not constitute improper deliberation since deliberation is defined as communication

allegations.summary: Commission allegedly failed to notify a member of his dismissal from the Commission.
allegations.key_passage: Third, the Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body provide notice of dismissal to an individual.

allegations.summary: Minutes of the June 12 meeting allegedly were falsified or inaccurate because they omit a member's question about his reappointment.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Commission did not discuss Mr. Mavrides' question, it was not required to include it in the meeting minutes.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
